generatedProse.concept-context: In sport coaching and physical education you learn the conventions by reading the subject's writing as a writer, not only for its content. Read a well-regarded coaching review or a reflective case a second time and watch how it is made. Notice how a session is described, how judgements about a performer are hedged, how practice and theory are tied together, and how earlier work is cited to build a case. These recurring choices are the conventions. Noticing them across the School of Sport, from a biomechanics report to a coaching log, lets you write towards them rather than waiting to be told the rules.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching and physical education students are each handed an unfamiliar coaching journal article and asked how writing is done in the subject.

Tom reads it once, for content, and reports what the study found about a training method. Asked about its conventions, he can only say it was 'formal and quite hard'. The article has been read, but only as information. Its conventions stayed invisible, because he never looked at how it was written.

Amara reads it twice. The second time she ignores the findings and watches the writing: the coach-researcher rarely appears, judgements are hedged and tied to evidence, practice is linked to theory, and earlier models are woven into the argument rather than listed. She can now name four conventions of coaching writing and write towards them.

Both students read the same article. Only Amara read it as a writer, and so could see the conventions Tom missed.
generatedProse.summary: The conventions of the School of Sport are learned by reading its writing as a writer: reading a coaching review or report again for how it is made, noticing the structure, hedging, voice and use of evidence, and writing towards them. You can now explain that way of reading, appraise a piece against the aspects that reveal its conventions, and choose what to notice in an unfamiliar article. The final lesson puts this to work on writing with a critical edge.

check.body: In the worked example, why could Amara name the subject's conventions when Tom could not?

items.text: She read the article a second time, watching the writing rather than the findings.
She already knew more about the training method than Tom.
She found the article easier to understand.
She agreed with the study's conclusions.

feedback.correct: That's right. A second reading focused on how the article was written made coaching's conventions visible.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what Amara DID differently with the article.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara could name the conventions because she read the article again, watching how it was written rather than what it found.
